title: NJ Driver's Manual – Chapter 4
subtitle: Rules of the Road
note: Based on the 2025 NJ Driver's Manual, Chapter 4. Verify all answers against the current manual before your exam.

questions.q: What is the default speed limit in a business or residential district in NJ unless otherwise posted?
opts: 15 mph
25 mph
35 mph
45 mph
questions.exp: The default speed limit in a business or residential district in NJ is 25 mph. Always obey posted signs, which may set a different limit.

questions.q: What is the default speed limit on a state highway in NJ unless otherwise posted?
opts: 35 mph
45 mph
50 mph
55 mph
questions.exp: The default speed limit on NJ state highways is 55 mph. Some sections of major expressways may be posted at 65 mph.

questions.q: The '3-second rule' is used to determine:
opts: How long to signal before turning
A safe following distance behind the vehicle ahead
The time to remain stopped at a red light
The maximum time to complete a lane change
questions.exp: The 3-second rule establishes a safe following distance. Pick a fixed roadside object, watch the vehicle ahead pass it, then count — you should not reach that point in fewer than 3 seconds.

questions.q: To apply the 3-second following distance rule, you should:
opts: Count 3 seconds from when you first see a hazard
Watch the vehicle ahead pass a fixed object, then count at least 3 seconds before you reach that same point
Stay exactly 3 car lengths behind at all speeds
Allow 3 seconds of reaction time added to braking distance
questions.exp: Choose any fixed roadside marker (a sign, tree, or shadow). The moment the vehicle ahead passes it, start counting. If you reach the marker in fewer than 3 seconds, you are following too closely.

questions.q: In NJ, what is the minimum distance you must park from a fire hydrant?
opts: 5 feet
10 feet
15 feet
25 feet
questions.exp: You must park at least 10 feet from a fire hydrant in NJ. Blocking a hydrant can delay firefighters responding to an emergency.

questions.q: How far from a stop sign must you NOT park in NJ?
opts: 10 feet
15 feet
25 feet
50 feet
questions.exp: NJ law prohibits parking within 25 feet of a stop sign, intersection, or crosswalk. Parked vehicles at those locations block visibility for both drivers and pedestrians.

questions.q: When making a right turn, you should approach from:
opts: The left lane
The center lane
The rightmost available lane
Any lane that is clear
questions.exp: Begin and end a right turn in the rightmost lane. Approaching from any other lane creates crossing conflicts with other vehicles.

questions.q: When making a left turn on a two-way road, you should approach from:
opts: The rightmost lane
The lane nearest to the center line
The center turn lane if one exists, otherwise the lane nearest the center
Any lane, provided you signal
questions.exp: For left turns, approach from the lane nearest the center line (or the center turn lane if one is marked). Complete the turn into the nearest left lane of the cross street.

questions.q: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right in NJ?
opts: Never — passing on the right is always prohibited
When the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is enough room on the right
On a one-way road with two or more lanes
Both when the vehicle is turning left and on multi-lane one-way roads
questions.exp: Passing on the right is permitted when (1) the vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn and there is room to pass safely, or (2) the road is a one-way street with two or more lanes.

questions.q: Before changing lanes, the correct sequence of actions is:
opts: Signal, speed up, change lanes
Check mirrors, signal, check blind spot, change lanes smoothly when safe
Change quickly — the less time in the blind spot the better
Signal and change simultaneously
questions.exp: Always signal your intent first, check all mirrors, physically check the blind spot (look over your shoulder), then change lanes smoothly when the gap is safe.

questions.q: In NJ, you must signal before a turn at least how far in advance?
opts: 50 feet
100 feet
200 feet
500 feet
questions.exp: NJ law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before making a turn or lane change. This gives other drivers time to react to your intentions.

questions.q: A 'No Standing' zone means:
opts: You may never stop for any reason
You may stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers only — the driver must remain at the wheel and be ready to move
You may park if the driver stays in the vehicle
No parking during peak hours
questions.exp: No Standing allows only a momentary stop to board or discharge passengers; the driver must remain ready to move immediately. No Loading/Unloading of freight is permitted.

questions.q: A 'No Stopping' zone means:
opts: No parking, but standing and loading are allowed
You may stop only if a traffic signal requires it or in an emergency
You may stop briefly with driver in the vehicle
Stopping is prohibited at all times for all purposes except emergencies or traffic conditions
questions.exp: A No Stopping zone is the most restrictive — no stopping is allowed for any reason except compliance with a traffic control device, a law enforcement officer's direction, or an emergency.

questions.q: In NJ, headlights are required:
opts: Only when it is completely dark
From sunset to sunrise, and any time visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less
Only on highways
From 10 PM to 6 AM
questions.exp: NJ law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever weather or other conditions (fog, rain, smoke) reduce visibility to 500 feet or less.

questions.q: NJ law requires headlights to be on whenever:
opts: The radio is on
Windshield wipers are in use due to rain, snow, or other precipitation
The engine is running
You are within 500 feet of a school
questions.exp: NJ's 'Wipers On — Lights On' law requires headlights to be illuminated any time the windshield wipers are being used due to precipitation. This increases visibility for all road users.

questions.q: Your vehicle's horn should be used:
opts: To express frustration at slow traffic
To greet people you know
Only as a warning — to alert others to avoid a collision
Freely to communicate with other drivers
questions.exp: The horn is a safety device, not a communication tool. Use it only to warn other drivers or pedestrians of a hazard — not to express anger or impatience.

questions.q: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
opts: Only when the gate is fully down
Only when a train is visibly approaching
When warning lights flash, the gate is lowering, a crossing guard signals you, or a train is approaching or audible
Only when a flagman is present
questions.exp: Stop at railroad crossings whenever warning lights flash, a gate is lowering, a crossing guard signals you to stop, or you can see or hear an approaching train.

questions.q: How close to the nearest rail may you stop at a railroad crossing?
opts: Right at the rail
At least 10 feet
At least 15 feet
At least 25 feet
questions.exp: NJ law requires stopping at least 15 feet from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing. Never stop on the tracks — if traffic ahead is backed up, wait behind the crossing.

questions.q: On a multi-lane highway, slower traffic should:
opts: Drive in the left (passing) lane
Alternate lanes frequently
Stay in the right lane and allow faster traffic to pass on the left
Use the center lane
questions.exp: Keep right except to pass. Slower vehicles should remain in the right lane(s). Impeding traffic by driving slowly in the left lane is illegal in NJ.

questions.q: When parking facing downhill with a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
opts: Away from the curb
Toward (into) the curb
Straight ahead
To the left regardless of direction
questions.exp: Facing downhill: turn wheels toward (into) the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the tire will contact the curb and stop it. Engage the parking brake and leave in Park (or reverse for manual).

questions.q: When parking facing uphill with a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
opts: Toward (into) the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
To the right regardless of direction
questions.exp: Facing uphill with a curb: turn wheels away from the curb (toward the road). If the vehicle rolls back, the tire will catch the curb. Engage the parking brake.

questions.q: The hand signal for a left turn is:
opts: Left arm bent upward at the elbow
Left arm extended straight out to the left
Right arm out the window pointing left
Left hand out window pointing down
questions.exp: Left turn: extend the left arm straight out horizontally through the window. This is the standard hand signal recognized in NJ.

questions.q: The hand signal for a right turn is:
opts: Right arm extended out
Left arm extended straight to the left
Left arm bent upward at the elbow (90°)
Left arm pointing downward
questions.exp: Right turn: extend the left arm out the window and bend it upward at a 90° angle at the elbow (hand pointing up). This is the standard hand signal.

questions.q: The hand signal for slowing down or stopping is:
opts: Both hands raised
Left arm pointing straight up
Left arm bent downward at the elbow (hand pointing down)
Right arm out the window
questions.exp: Slowing/stopping: extend the left arm out the window and bend it downward at a 90° angle (hand pointing toward the ground).

questions.q: In NJ, what is the legal BAC limit for drivers under the age of 21?
questions.exp: NJ enforces a zero-tolerance policy for underage drivers: a BAC of 0.01% or higher (essentially any detectable alcohol) results in a DWI charge for drivers under 21.

questions.q: The legal BAC limit for commercial vehicle (CDL) drivers in NJ is:
questions.exp: Commercial drivers are held to a stricter standard: a BAC of 0.04% or higher while operating a commercial vehicle constitutes DWI in NJ, half the limit for regular drivers.

questions.q: NJ law prohibits which of the following while driving?
opts: Using a hands-free Bluetooth device
Using a handheld mobile phone or device for any purpose
Listening to music through a car stereo
Using a built-in GPS navigation screen
questions.exp: NJ bans all use of handheld electronic devices while driving (calling, texting, browsing). Hands-free devices are permitted. Violations carry significant fines and points.

questions.q: Traffic fines in a designated work (construction) zone in NJ are:
opts: Reduced because the road is under construction
The same as in any other zone
Doubled
Tripled for commercial vehicles
questions.exp: In NJ work zones, all motor vehicle fines are doubled. Workers are at risk, and higher fines deter dangerous driving through these zones.

questions.q: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching from behind while you are stopped at a red light, you should:
opts: Run the red light immediately to clear the way
Stay stopped until the light turns green, then pull to the right and stop
Remain in place — do not move until you can safely pull to the right
Back up to create space
questions.exp: Never run a red light for an emergency vehicle. Remain stopped, and as soon as it is safe, pull to the right of the intersection and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.q: After an emergency vehicle with lights and siren passes you, you should:
opts: Follow closely behind it for guidance
Wait at least 30 seconds before moving
Not follow within 300–500 feet of the emergency vehicle; wait until it is safely clear
Resume normal speed immediately
questions.exp: Do not follow an emergency vehicle within 300–500 feet while its lights and siren are active. Other emergency vehicles may be following, and the scene ahead may be dangerous.

questions.q: In NJ, you may make a U-turn:
opts: At any intersection if traffic allows
Only on one-way streets
Where it can be made safely and is not prohibited by posted signs or law
Only if no vehicles are within 200 feet
questions.exp: U-turns are permitted where they can be completed safely and where signs don't prohibit them. They are forbidden in business districts, near hills, curves, bridges, tunnels, and near railroad crossings.

questions.q: If your wheels drop off the edge of the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:
opts: Immediately jerk the steering wheel back onto the road
Brake hard to stop on the shoulder
Ease off the gas, hold the wheel straight, slow down gradually, then steer gently back onto the pavement
Accelerate to regain traction
questions.exp: Never jerk back onto the road at speed — your vehicle can roll over. Instead, ease off the gas, keep the vehicle straight and controlled on the shoulder, slow down, and then gently steer back onto the pavement.

questions.q: You must dim your high beams to low beams:
opts: Only in fog
Whenever another vehicle is within 500 feet approaching from the front, or within 200–300 feet of a vehicle you are following
Only when directed by road signs
Only after midnight
questions.exp: NJ law requires switching to low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 200–300 feet when following another vehicle. High beams blind other drivers.

questions.q: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be no more than how far from the curb?
opts: 6 inches
12 inches
18 inches
24 inches
questions.exp: When parallel parked, your vehicle must be within 6 inches of the curb (NJ standard). Parking too far out creates a hazard for passing traffic.

questions.q: When entering a highway from an on-ramp, you should:
opts: Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap
Enter at a slow speed to show caution
Accelerate in the merge lane (acceleration lane) to match highway speed before merging
Use your horn to alert highway traffic
questions.exp: The acceleration lane is designed for you to reach highway speed before merging. Entering too slowly disrupts traffic flow and increases the risk of rear-end collisions.

questions.q: When exiting a highway, you should:
opts: Brake hard as soon as you see the exit sign
Move into the exit lane in advance and begin slowing on the exit ramp, not on the main roadway
Signal and brake simultaneously on the main roadway
Exit at full highway speed to match the ramp's curve
questions.exp: Move to the exit lane well in advance. Braking on the highway's main lanes (instead of the exit ramp) is dangerous because drivers behind you expect normal highway speeds.

questions.q: In NJ, 'Driving While Intoxicated' (DWI) for drivers 21 and older is defined as a BAC of:
opts: 0.05% or higher
0.06% or higher
0.08% or higher
0.10% or higher
questions.exp: A BAC of 0.08% or higher is the legal threshold for DWI for drivers aged 21 and over. First-offense DWI in NJ carries significant fines, license suspension, and possible jail time.

questions.q: Which of the following actions is permitted while driving in NJ?
opts: Holding a cell phone to your ear to make a call
Sending a text message at a red light
Using a hands-free (Bluetooth) device to talk
Browsing social media at a stop sign
questions.exp: Hands-free phone use is permitted while driving in NJ. Any handheld use — including at traffic lights or stop signs — is prohibited and subject to fines.

questions.q: When may you legally cross a double solid yellow center line on a two-lane road?
opts: Never — not for any reason
To pass a slow-moving farm vehicle if no traffic is oncoming
To turn left into a driveway or side road
To avoid a pothole or debris in your lane
questions.exp: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing, but you may still cross them to turn left into a driveway, side road, or alley. The restriction applies to passing, not to left turns.

questions.q: A green traffic light gives you permission to proceed, but you must still:
opts: Immediately accelerate through the intersection
Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection or crosswalk
Check for cross traffic only if the light just turned green
Flash your headlights to warn cross traffic
questions.exp: Green means you may proceed — not that you must proceed. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians already lawfully in the intersection, and to emergency vehicles.

questions.q: The speed limit near a school in NJ when children are present is:
opts: 10 mph
15 mph
25 mph
As posted by the school zone signs
questions.exp: School zone speed limits are posted and vary by location. Drivers must obey the posted school zone speed when warning lights are active or children are present.
